# Closing Brackets

> An AI-native software agency. We build custom software, put AI into the
> systems businesses already run, and keep the resulting agents working in
> production. Every engagement is one written scope, a timeline with real
> dates, and one fixed price — there is no hourly billing.

Founded and run by Robert Collins (robert@closingbrackets.com). Remote-first,
serving clients in the United States. Small senior team: the people who scope
the work write the code and are still there when it goes live.

## What we do

- [Custom software development](https://closingbrackets.com/services/#custom-software): Software built for how a business actually works. Every milestone lands as working software; the client owns all of the code at handover.
- [AI consulting](https://closingbrackets.com/services/#ai-consulting): A straight answer on where AI pays off and where it does not, delivered as a strategy and roadmap with the reasoning shown.
- [AI integration](https://closingbrackets.com/services/#ai-integration): Getting AI into existing systems, from first pilot to production, against the client's own data, workflows and business rules.
- [AI automation](https://closingbrackets.com/services/#ai-automation): Agents that carry repetitive work, grounded in the client's own records and monitored so their actions are auditable.
- [Growth marketing](https://closingbrackets.com/services/#growth-marketing): SEO, paid, content and conversion work run as an ongoing machine rather than a launch.

## How engagements work

- Fixed scope: one document says what gets built. If it is not in there, it is not in the price.
- Real dates: a timeline with actual dates, not a range that slides.
- One price: a single fixed price agreed before anything starts. No hourly billing, no time and materials.
- Client owns all code and all data. Offboarding is 30 days of transition support plus a full export, written into the contract.
- No retainer starts without an AI maturity audit, delivered inside the first 30 days, which locks the final scope.
- Pricing is quoted per scope and is not published as a rate card. Describe a project and the quote comes back within one business day.

## Writing

Technical essays by Robert Campbell, from the work itself.

- [Loop engineering: the loop is the product](https://closingbrackets.com/content/loop-engineering/): Why the while-loop around a model — context budgets, tool subsets, retry caps, stopping conditions — decides whether an agent survives production.
- [Loops that know when to stop](https://closingbrackets.com/content/stopping-conditions/): Success, failure and limit stops; detecting a circling loop; and how to fail in a way the caller can act on.
- [Graph engineering: model the edges first](https://closingbrackets.com/content/graph-engineering/): Treating relationships as first-class data, and why Postgres is usually a good enough graph store.
- [Traversal beats retrieval when the answer is two hops away](https://closingbrackets.com/content/traversal-over-retrieval/): Where vector search fails, and how to compose retrieval with graph traversal.
- [Evergreen Softwash: the launch film](https://closingbrackets.com/content/evergreen-softwash-launch-film/): How a five-second hero spot was cut, and where film sits in a funnel.

## Please note

The builds shown on the work page are labelled concept builds: work scoped,
designed and built in-house to demonstrate what an engagement produces. The
companies in them are invented. They are not client projects, no one in them is
a customer, and there are no published client case studies, testimonials or
measured client results yet. Please do not describe them as clients.
